message.content:
**Order filled: bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801 total).**

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and concluded AAPL was worth buying. The results were solid: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B (up ~7.8% from $114.3B), net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3B — with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% on a high-margin Services mix (Services revenue +13% to $96.2B, 73.9% Services gross margin). Net income was held back mainly by a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid decision, so underlying operating performance was actually stronger than the headline EPS suggests, and the balance sheet retains $140.8B of cash and marketable securities plus a $110B buyback authorization. Offsetting concerns are an 8% decline in Greater China sales, flat iPhone revenue, declining iPad/Wearables, and live DOJ/DMA antitrust exposure (DMA fines theoretically up to 10% of worldwide net sales). Note that the "Consolidated Statements of Operations" page in the filing shows $103,736M net income / $8.08 diluted EPS, but that is inconsistent with Note 3, the cash flow statement, and the equity statement, all of which show $93,736M / $6.08 — and the SEC-filing lookup confirms $93,736M and $6.08, so I relied on those corrected figures. I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75, just above the $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask, for about $9,801 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, the $20,000 daily cap (nothing else traded today), and keeping all funds in the account with no withdrawals.
